paper.title: The Simeck Family of Lightweight Block Ciphers

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm description; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: Simeck32/64 and Simeck64/128 encrypt the paper's own test vectors to the published ciphertexts (2 of 2)
18 further vectors (9 per variant) that the Crypto++ file labels "SIMECK reference implementation" match (18 of 18, 20 of 20 in all)
decrypting each of the 20 ciphertexts returns the plaintext (20 of 20 round trips)

expected_values_source.what: the Crypto++ test-vector file simeck.txt: 2 entries labelled "SIMECK test vector" (the paper's vectors; in the paper's word notation) and 18 labelled "SIMECK reference implementation"; the round-constant bit sequences (32 bits for Simeck32/64, 44 bits for Simeck64/128) come from the Crypto++ source file simeck.cpp
expected_values_source.note: the paper PDF itself was not fetched (eprint 403); the 18 reference-implementation vectors are as labelled by Crypto++ and were not checked against the authors' repository. Data copied as numbers; no code was copied

negative_control: built with SIMECK_ROT5=4 (rotation by 4 instead of 5 in f), 0 of 2 paper vectors and 0 of 20 vectors match, program exits 1
not_checked: security claims, hardware area or power figures
whether the 18 reference-implementation vectors are the authors' own outputs (taken as labelled)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces the published Simeck32/64 and Simeck64/128 test vectors and 18 more labelled reference vectors. It does not show the cipher is secure.
